# The quarter bound for five positive interval fibers

Let C be a convex body in `R x R` with exactly five nonempty integer
fibers, all positive-length intervals. Assume its actual mixed centroid
has an integer first coordinate. Then that coordinate is necessarily
the middle of the five indices, and the actual centroid belongs to S
and has mixed halfspace depth at least 1/4. Every oblique cap and every
captured/excluded fiber pattern is included below.

## 0. The only possible integer mean is the central index

The five indices are consecutive, and positivity puts their weighted
mean strictly between the extreme indices. Suppose an integer mean
were the second index from the left. After integer translation and
continuous length scaling, the indices and widths would be

    (-1,0,1,2,3),  (1+2t+3u,s,1,t,u),  t,u>0.

Here the first width is forced by the weighted integer mean zero.
Concavity at the next three indices requires

    s>=1+t+3u/2,   s<=2-t,   t>=(1+u)/2.

The first two imply `t<=1/2-3u/4`, contradicting the last because
u is positive. Reflection excludes the second index from the right.
Thus the middle index is the only possible integer mean. This also
shows that no off-center positive five-fiber pattern was omitted.

## 1. The exact width parameter space

Translate the integer coordinates so the indices are `-2,-1,0,1,2`
and the centroid's base coordinate is zero. As in
`candidate b9d705e0e5ad374f`, move any nonvertical
containing cap inward to the centroid and apply an invertible affine
fiber shear so that the centroid is `(0,0)` and the cap is `x>=0`.
Write its interval endpoints as l_i,r_i and lengths as w_i.

The integer mean identity is

    w_-1+2w_-2=w_1+2w_2>0.

Scale all continuous lengths so this common quantity is one. Then

    (w_-2,w_-1,w_0,w_1,w_2)
       =(a,1-2a,c,1-2b,b).

Concavity of the widths gives exactly

    0<a,b<=1/3,
    1-a-b<=c<=2-5a,
    1-a-b<=c<=2-5b.                                    (1)

For the individual bounds on a,b, the three displayed concavity
inequalities first give `4a-b<=1`, `4b-a<=1`; if a is the larger of
the two, `3a<=4a-b<=1`, and likewise for b. Put

    A=a+b, B=a^2+b^2,
    M=c+2-A,
    Q=sum_i w_i^2=c^2+2-4A+5B.                         (2)

The true continuous-mean identity gives

    sum_i w_i r_i=Q/2.

Jensen for the concave upper endpoints and convex lower endpoints,
at the weighted integer mean zero, gives

    r_0>=Q/(2M)>0,  l_0<=-Q/(2M)<0.                   (3)

The central fiber is therefore always properly cut.

## 2. No wholly captured fiber, or a captured inner neighbor

If no fiber is wholly captured, the elementary finite-family estimate
from Section 7 of the four-fiber note applies:

    cap_mass>=Q/(2 max_i w_i)>=M/(1+sqrt(5))>M/4.

This estimate needs no all-fiber straddling assumption and allows
negative upper endpoints at wholly excluded fibers.

Suppose fiber 1 is wholly captured, so `l_1>=0`. Convexity and (3)
give `l_2>=2l_1-l_0>0`, hence fiber 2 is captured too. The captured
block has mass `1-b`, and (1) implies

    4(1-b)-M>=a+2b>0.

Indeed use `c<=2-5b` in `M=c+2-a-b`. Thus the block alone pays more
than M/4. The analogous left block has mass `1-a` and satisfies
`4(1-a)-M>=2a+b>0`. These cases cover every pattern with a captured
inner neighbor. The central fiber cannot be captured by (3).

It remains only to consider captured subsets `{2}`, `{-2}`, and
`{-2,2}`. Reflection exchanges the two singleton cases.

## 3. Only the right outer fiber is wholly captured

Here `r_2>=b`. Concavity gives `r_2<=2r_1-r_0`, hence `r_1>0`.
The exact cap mass F is

    F=(r_-2)_+ +(r_-1)_+ +r_0+r_1+b.

Discarding possibly negative upper endpoints on the left, and then
eliminating r_2 by concavity, gives

    Q/2
      <=a(r_-2)_+ +(1-2a)(r_-1)_+
                           +(c-b)r_0+r_1
      <=K(F-b),

where `K=max(1,c-b)`. The last step uses `a<=1`, `1-2a<=1`, and
the positivity of r_0,r_1. Consequently

    F>=Q/(2K)+b.                                       (4)

To prove (4) exceeds M/4, it suffices to show
`E=2Q+4bK-KM>0`.

If K=1, expansion gives

    E=2c^2-c+2-7a-3b+10a^2+10b^2.

The function `2c^2-c` increases for `c>=1/3`, and (1) gives
`c>=1-a-b>=1/3`. Therefore

    E>=3-10a-6b+12a^2+4ab+12b^2.

This last quadratic decreases in a on the entire square
`0<=a,b<=1/3`, since its a derivative is at most `-2/3`. Setting
`a=1/3` therefore gives the lower bound

    E>=12(b-7/36)^2+59/108>0.

If K=c-b>=1, expansion instead gives

    E=c^2-2c+ac+6bc+4-8a-6b+10a^2+5b^2-ab.

Its c derivative is nonnegative for `c>=1+b`. Substitution of that
lower endpoint gives

    E>=3-7a+10a^2+12b^2>=16/9>0,

because the a quadratic decreases on `[0,1/3]` and attains its
minimum there at `a=1/3`. This proves the right-only captured case;
reflection proves the left-only one.

## 4. Both outer fibers are wholly captured

Now r_-1,r_0,r_1 are positive, by (3) and concavity at both sides.
The exact cap mass is

    F=r_-1+r_0+r_1+A.

Eliminating both outer upper endpoints from the true moment identity
uses the two equal coefficients forced by the integer mean:

    Q/2<=r_-1+r_1+(c-A)r_0<=K(F-A),
    K=max(1,c-A).

Thus `F>=Q/(2K)+A`. Again it suffices to check
`E=2Q+4AK-KM>0`.

For K=1,

    E=2c^2-c+2-3A+10B
      >=3-6A+2A^2+10B
      >=3-6A+7A^2
       =7(A-3/7)^2+12/7>0.

The first inequality uses `c>=1-A>=1/3`, and the second uses
`B>=A^2/2`. For K=c-A>=1,

    E=c^2-2c+6Ac+4-6A-5A^2+10B.

Its c derivative is nonnegative for `c>=1+A`; at that endpoint it
equals `3+2A^2+10B>0`. This closes the last captured-tail pattern.

## 5. Ambient halfspaces, boundary mass, and membership

Every nonvertical halfspace through the actual centroid has been
handled after a lattice-preserving fiber shear. Every containing
halfspace contains its parallel translate through that centroid.
Nonvertical boundaries have zero mixed length, while all equalities
at l_i=0 or r_i=0 were explicitly permitted by the cap formulas.

A vertical closed halfspace through the centroid has mass either
`1-a+c` or `1-b+c`. Each is larger than M/2, since twice that mass
minus M is `c+b-a` or `c+a-b`, and

    c-|a-b|>=1-a-b-|a-b|=1-2max(a,b)>=1/3.

This computation includes the entire central fiber on the boundary.
The actual mixed centroid lies in C by convexity and has integer
base coordinate zero, so it is a point of S. These observations
complete the deterministic all-halfspace quarter bound. QED.
